summary: Underground poster pairs a gourmet salmon plate with a bottle of formaldehyde being poured on it, claiming all Scottish supermarket salmon comes from factory farms with endemic flesh-eating sea lice and is doused in toxic chemicals. It targets general commuters, challenging 'gourmet' industry framing.

claims.claim: All Scottish salmon sold in UK supermarkets comes from factory farms
claims.notes: Absolute 'all' claim; 'factory farm' is undefined and contestable. Some supermarket salmon is organic or higher-welfare certified.
Sea lice are widespread on Scottish farms, but 'flesh-eating' and 'endemic' need documentary support and careful definition.

claims.claim: Salmon are doused in toxic chemicals including formaldehyde, deltamethrin and hydrogen peroxide
claims.notes: 'Doused' implies routine, heavy use. Need current usage data, authorisation status and whether formaldehyde is used in Scotland.

claims.claim: Image/text: salmon is 'seasoned' with a cocktail of chemicals (formaldehyde poured on plate)
claims.notes: Implies chemical residues on the fillet served to consumers. Treatments are applied to live fish in pens, not the plate.

claims.claim: They say Scottish salmon is 'gourmet dining'
claims.notes: Attributed to an unnamed 'they'. Identify actual industry or retailer wording to avoid a straw-man charge.

attacks.quote: Scottish salmon is among the most tightly regulated food in the world. This scaremongering misleads shoppers and attacks thousands of hard-working coastal jobs.
No formaldehyde is poured on your dinner. Treatments are vet-prescribed, licensed, and food is tested for residues. This is vegan propaganda.
Complainants allege the ad misleads by implying consumers eat chemical residues, and that 'all' Scottish salmon is factory farmed, which is unsubstantiated.
Animal rights campaign's tube ad implies salmon is soaked in formaldehyde. Regulators and farmers say that's misleading.
Is my supermarket salmon actually laced with formaldehyde? Or is this another activist scare tactic? I'm not sure I believe either side.
We need substantiation for the health and safety implications in this creative before approving it for display on our network.

risks.issue: Implied chemical contamination of the food (formaldehyde poured on plate, 'seasoned') could be read as a food safety claim
'All Scottish salmon' absolute claim with undefined 'factory farm' and no evidence held
'Doused in toxic chemicals' overstates frequency and dosage; formaldehyde use in Scotland unverified
Possible reputational or legal exposure from trade bodies or named producers if claim taken to cover all farms
Body copy is tiny and low-contrast, so qualifying detail is unreadable in transit
No sources or footnote on the poster for the statistics
'They say' attribution unclear, so 'gourmet dining' may read as a straw man
Public may disbelieve or feel manipulated if the chemical-on-plate image feels exaggerated

fixes.fix: Make clear treatments are applied to live fish in pens. Change 'seasoned' line or add 'on the farm' so it can't read as residue on the plate.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: Before it reaches your plate, it's been dosed with a cocktail of chemicals. Lemon and dill not included.

fixes.fix: Define 'factory farm' in the evidence pack, then narrow the wording to what is provable, such as 'most' or 'almost all', with a source.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: Nearly all Scottish salmon in UK supermarkets is raised in crowded open-net pens where sea lice are rife.

fixes.fix: Replace 'doused' with 'treated with' and cite regulator or industry data for each named chemical's current use in Scottish farms.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: Farmed salmon are routinely treated with chemicals including hydrogen peroxide and deltamethrin to fight sea lice.

fixes.fix: Verify current authorised use in Scottish farms. If not verifiable, drop it from the copy and the bottle label.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: Swap the bottle label to hydrogen peroxide, whose use is well documented.

fixes.fix: Add short source line and enlarge body copy. Put the full evidence on the website landing page.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: Source: [named regulator/industry data, year]. Evidence at endfactoryfarming.com.

working: Strong 'Don't Buy It' double meaning set against the 'gourmet dining' claim
Striking, instantly readable image of poison poured on fine dining
Clear, memorable contrast between luxury branding and farm reality
Elegant, high-end styling makes the disgust angle stand out on the Underground
Clear branding and URL for follow-up
legal_flags: Absolute 'All Scottish salmon' claim needs documentary evidence held before publication
Possible defamation or malicious falsehood exposure if producers or trade bodies are identifiable
Implied food safety or health claim via formaldehyde-on-plate imagery
Verify formaldehyde use in Scottish salmon farming and each chemical's regulatory status before launch
No reference documents supplied, so CAP Code and ASA precedent must be checked against source documents
